title: Zero hitting probability from an isolated vertex
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $	ext{Fin}(n)$. For distinct vertices $s,t\in\text{Fin}(n)$, if $s$ has no outgoing neighbors in the digraph defined by $r$, then for every natural number $k$, the $k$-step probability of hitting $t$ from $s$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: A decidable relation r on Fin(n), defining the digraph.
Distinct vertices s and t in Fin(n).
The out-neighborhood of s has cardinality zero.
